title: The routing model, the index manager and transit callbacks

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: In an interview you are asked how the OR-Tools routing library models a 40-stop delivery tour, compared with a MIP that has one binary per ordered pair of stops. Which answer is accurate?

options.text: It writes the same binaries and subtour rows, then solves them all by branch and bound
options.says: The routing library writes no subtour rows and runs no branch and bound; it searches over successor variables.

options.text: It keeps a successor per stop and improves the routes by local search, with no bound
options.says: Right: next_i per stop, a first solution, then local search; it reports no bound or gap.

options.text: It keeps one successor variable per stop and always proves the final tour optimal
options.says: The routing search reports no bound, so it proves nothing about optimality.

options.text: It writes the binaries but drops every subtour row, since local search never forms loops
options.says: It writes no binaries at all; its path constraints keep each route connected.

origin.section: A Routing Model Chooses a Successor for Every Stop

questions.stem: A two-van model has 6 nodes with the depot at node 0. Its transit callback reads matrix[from_index][to_index] without converting the indices. What does it read on an arc into a van's end?

options.text: Row and column 0, since an end index is the same number as the depot node
options.says: End indices come after the visits and the starts; they are not 0.

options.text: The right entry, since indices and nodes always match on a two-van model
options.says: They match for visits, but the second van's start and both ends get indices of their own.

options.text: The start's entry, since each van's end shares one index with its start
options.says: Each van has a separate start index and end index.

options.text: A column past the matrix, since ends are numbered after every visit
options.says: Right: with 6 nodes and 2 vans the ends are indices 7 and 8, beyond a 6-column matrix.

origin.section: The Index Manager Translates Between Your Nodes and the Solver's Indices

questions.stem: A routing service hands you drive times in minutes with decimals, such as 12.4 and 7.75. How should they reach the routing model?

options.text: Multiply by 100, round to integers, and divide the objective by 100 to report it
options.says: Right: scale, round, and divide back; the scale keeps the precision you care about.

options.text: Return the floats as they are, since the solver rounds each arc to whole minutes
options.says: A float return is not rounded for you: the solve fails with SystemError.

options.text: Cut each one down with int(), since dropping decimals never changes the best tour
options.says: Changing the costs can change the tour; the lesson's tenths-of-a-minute model picked a different, shorter one.

options.text: Round each to whole minutes, since finer units would overflow the integer costs
options.says: Costs are 64-bit integers; tenths of a minute fit easily, and gave a truly shorter tour.
